acquisition.why: Cold email to UK limited companies is legal, and SEO pages like 'ZoomInfo alternative' can be run by agents. Deliverability needs monitoring and corporate-vs-sole-trader screening is required [E].

onboarding.why: Self-serve signup and a free-leads trial need no human.

delivery.why: Serving the software is automated, but getting and keeping a lawful, accurate B2B dataset needs ongoing sourcing, licensing and quality work [E].

support.why: Agents can handle FAQs and data-accuracy complaints. GDPR subject-access and erasure requests need human sign-off.

scores.R_why: Building a credible verified contact database is capital- and data-intensive. UK GDPR legitimate-interest and erasure duties fall on him as data controller. A £300 test and 6-8 h/week cannot compete with ZoomInfo, Apollo or Cognism. The one realistic angle is reselling via API, which leaves a thin margin [E].
scores.M_why: Saturated market where cheap players like Apollo bundle data with AI outbound tooling. Data is commoditised, and the ICO is increasingly scrutinising data brokers.
scores.one_line: Real founder-reported traction in 2 videos, but the claims are promotional (the guest sells UpLead). Capital, data sourcing and GDPR liability make this a poor fit for a £300 UK side project.

acquisition.why: Inbound via SEO, content, app stores and paid ads aimed at trainers is feasible. Partnerships with gyms or certification bodies would help. No channel was evidenced in the source [E].

delivery.why: LLM summarisation of client logs runs unattended. Coaches review the output themselves.

support.why: Agents handle most issues. Data-protection queries about client health data need human checks.

scores.R_why: An MVP is buildable by a technical solo founder at low cost. However, UK personal trainers are mostly sole traders, so cold email is illegal and acquisition must be inbound. Fitness and health data counts as special category data under UK GDPR. At about £10/month, many users are needed [E].
scores.M_why: Trainerize, TrueCoach, Everfit and others are adding AI features. Coaches can also use ChatGPT directly, so a thin wrapper is easily commoditised [E].
scores.one_line: Buildable and well suited to agents, but this is a hypothetical one-video idea. It is a thin AI wrapper in a market where incumbents are adding AI features, and £10/month needs scale [E].

acquisition.why: Inbound via Google Business Profile, local SEO, Facebook Marketplace and parent groups. Agents can manage listings and ads.

onboarding.why: Online booking and deposits can be automated. Site suitability and safety checks need human input.

delivery.why: Heavy physical delivery, setup, collection and cleaning, plus PIPA/RPII inspections.

support.why: Weather cancellations, damage disputes and on-the-day issues need a human.

scores.R_why: Weekend physical labour conflicts with a toddler and 6-8 h/week. Requires storage, a van, and public liability insurance. £300 only covers a few giant garden games. Bromley demand exists, but the work cannot be run by agents.
scores.M_why: UK bouncy castle and event hire is crowded and highly seasonal. The source itself reports competition rising after COVID.
scores.one_line: Well-evidenced real businesses across 10 videos, but delivery is entirely physical weekend labour. It fundamentally fails the agent-run, approve-only requirement.

acquisition.why: SEO and content sites, YouTube and newsletters are legal inbound channels that agents can produce. This depends on Google and platforms, and needs an audience.

onboarding.why: There is no customer onboarding; the merchant handles the customer.

delivery.why: Agents can produce content. Fulfilment is done by the merchant.

billing.why: Networks such as Awin and Impact pay commissions automatically.

scores.R_why: Cheap to start and runnable by agents. However, building a trusted audience takes many months. Financial products such as credit cards bring FCA financial-promotion rules. ASA disclosure is required.
scores.M_why: Since 2024, Google updates and AI Overviews have hammered affiliate SEO sites. AI-generated content floods every niche, and commission cuts are common [E].
scores.one_line: Highly automatable with zero fulfilment, but the evidence is vague (1 first-hand claim, no numbers). AI search and Google updates have badly eroded the affiliate content model in 2026 [E].

acquisition.why: Inbound via search, maps and aggregators.

onboarding.why: Online rental, ID checks and smart access are possible in unmanned facilities.

delivery.why: Physical property; maintenance, security and lien or abandoned-goods handling need humans.

billing.why: Automated recurring rent, with occasional arrears handling.

support.why: Access problems, damage and disputes need on-site humans.

scores.R_why: Needs hundreds of thousands to millions of pounds, plus UK land and planning in London. That is impossible with a £300 budget and part-time hours.
scores.M_why: UK self-storage is established (Big Yellow, Safestore) and is a property play. Headroom depends on finding a site.
scores.one_line: Real wealth stories, but the capital requirement is several orders of magnitude beyond Ricardo's means. Physical property cannot be agent-run.

acquisition.why: Consumer leads arrive via SEO inbound. Finding rental buyers relies on cold calls or walk-ins in the source. In the UK, tradespeople are often sole traders, so cold email is barred and calls need TPS/CTPS screening and a human. Email is possible only to Ltd firms.

onboarding.why: Negotiating deals, free trials and verifying the buyer answers calls (secret shopping) involve humans.

delivery.why: Once ranked, the site and call tracking run largely unattended. Agents can write content and monitor rankings.

billing.why: Stripe flat monthly fees. Payment chasing and disputes occur.

support.why: Lead-quality disputes and buyer churn need some human handling.

scores.R_why: Technical, low cost (domains and hosting under £300) and fits limited hours. However, ranking takes months, and Bromley and London are competitive. Fake Google Business Profiles breach policy. Buyer outreach needs a lawful channel: cold email to Ltd firms, or TPS-screened calls [E].
scores.M_why: UK search is dominated by Checkatrade, MyBuilder, Bark and Google Local Services Ads. AI Overviews and GBP crackdowns squeeze organic lead sites [E].
scores.one_line: Several first-hand operators report recurring revenue and low ongoing effort, with a good automated delivery core. UK buyer acquisition is the legal and human bottleneck, alongside SEO and GBP platform risk [E].

acquisition.why: Meta ads, TikTok and Pinterest content and gifting SEO are all inbound. Agents can produce content and run ads; CAC is rising.

delivery.why: Agents can draft writing and art (with human editing). Printing and mailing can go to a print-and-post API or fulfilment house, but sequencing quality needs checks [E].

support.why: Lost letters and cancellations can be handled mostly by agents.

scores.R_why: A £300 test is feasible: a handful of letters through a UK print-and-post API plus small ads. Royal Mail postage (stamps around £0.85+) erodes margin at a ~£10 price point. Content quality is time-consuming. UK gifting demand exists around Mother's Day [E].
scores.M_why: Niche, with a tangible-mail novelty that AI cannot fully substitute. Few UK players, but low barriers and copycats [E].
scores.one_line: Several first-hand businesses and a physical product whose delivery can be outsourced to a print-and-post API. Viable as a small UK test, but paid-acquisition CAC and postage are the key risks [E].

acquisition.why: Cold email to UK Ltd e-commerce brands is legal, and SEO, content and Shopify app listings are possible. Agents can run these.

onboarding.why: A web form collects competitor names and URLs.

delivery.why: Scheduled pulls from scrapers or the Meta Ad Library API plus LLM summaries run unattended. Quality spot-checks are needed.

support.why: Agents handle report questions and competitor changes; occasional scraper breakages need a human.

scores.R_why: Squarely within Ricardo's technical skills. Cost is around £5-20/month, so the test fits £300. The UK/EU Meta Ad Library has richer data. Scraping terms and sites blocking scrapers are a risk [E].
scores.M_why: Very low barrier and widely copied. Crowded by Semrush, Similarweb, Prisync, AdSpy and Foreplay, and buyers can now build it themselves with agents [E].
scores.one_line: Highly agent-runnable and cheap to test, but the evidence is mostly demos and hypothetical prices with no paying customers. Commoditisation means niche positioning (e.g. UK Shopify brands in one vertical) is essential [E].
